1 · Project Overview, Charter & Scope

Context, problem and solution

RA Cleaning Service is a small business providing residential and commercial cleaning. Enquiries currently arrive by phone, SMS and social media and are recorded by hand, so enquiries are missed, cleaners are double-booked and customer details are inconsistent. This project delivers an online booking and customer-management system: customers view services and book a clean online, the office manages bookings and allocates staff from one dashboard, and customers receive automatic email and SMS confirmations.

Development approach

We use a hybrid approach. Initiation, planning, design approval, testing and go-live are managed predictively with milestone gates, because the sponsor has a fixed budget and needs a firm launch date. Development runs as three two-week Agile sprints tracked on , because the owner and staff will only refine booking and dashboard requirements once they see working screens (a lesson from our Assessment 1 planning). Sprint reviews give the sponsor a controlled point to reprioritise without disturbing the overall baseline.

Work Breakdown Structure

The WBS decomposes the product into five deliverable areas and 20 work packages plus five milestones. Every work package is one ProjectLibre task and one Trello card with the same WBS code, so scope, schedule and tracking stay aligned.

2 · Schedule, Cost & Resources

ProjectLibre schedule

The ProjectLibre schedule runs for 68 working days, from Monday 3 August to Wednesday 4 November 2026, with finish-to-start dependencies, resources assigned to every activity and a saved baseline.

Milestones

MilestoneBaseline dateMeaningStatus (25 Sep)
M1 – Project plan approvedWed 12 Aug 2026Charter, plan and budget approved by sponsor – go/no-go gateComplete
M2 – Requirements & design approvedMon 31 Aug 2026Requirements, prototype and privacy review signed off – development may startComplete

M4 – Go-liveMon 26 Oct 2026System live for customersAt Risk
M5 – Project closedWed 04 Nov 2026Hypercare finished, sponsor sign-off, lessons learnedAt Risk

Critical path

The critical path is 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.3 → M1 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.4 → 2.5 → M2 → 3.1 → 3.2 → 3.3 → M3 → 4.1 → 4.2 → 4.3 → 4.5 → M4 → 5.1 → 5.2 → M5. These activities have zero float because each one needs the previous output: for example the privacy review needs the architecture design, and every sprint builds on the last. Activities off the critical path have float: the UI prototype (1 day), notification integration (3 days), staff training (3 days) and training materials (16 days).

A significant dependency

One significant dependency is Sprint 2 (3.2) → Sprint 3 (3.3). The booking-management dashboard cannot be built until the booking form and availability calendar exist, because the dashboard displays and allocates those bookings. Notification integration (3.4) and training materials (3.5) also wait on Sprint 2, which makes it the busiest node in the network.

If a critical activity is delayed

If a critical activity slips, every later milestone slips by the same amount unless time is recovered. This is happening now: Sprint 2 is forecast three days late, which would move go-live from 26 to 29 October and closure to 9 November. It would also shorten the gap between go-live and the busy pre-Christmas cleaning season, when staff have least time for training.

Cost and resources

Six costed roles deliver the work: Roshan as Project Manager, and a contracted UI/UX designer, web developer, junior developer and tester. Labour is estimated as duration × 8 hours × hourly rate, so cost is directly driven by the activities and durations in ProjectLibre: development is 44% of labour because the sprints are the longest activities and use the highest-rated resource. Labour totals $35,360; hosting, SMS credits, licences, security scanning and training materials add $1,880; a 10% contingency ($3,724) covers the top risks, giving an approved budget of $40,964. Key assumptions: rates are planning estimates, not quotes; sponsor time is not charged; GST is excluded; public holidays are not modelled.

Top three risks and responses

R01 Scope creep (16). The owner sees new ideas at every sprint demo. Response: mitigate – all requests go through the change register, are costed before decision, and the backlog is re-prioritised with MoSCoW so extras replace lower-value items rather than extend the sprint. CR-02 (online payment) was deferred under this rule.

R02 Double bookings (15). A booking system that double-books cleaners fails its core purpose. Response: mitigate – early prototyping of the calendar logic, 50 scripted test scenarios and a zero-Sev-1 go-live rule. This risk has partly occurred (one double-booking defect), which is why Sprint 2 is late.

R03 Single senior developer (15). All three sprints depend on one person. Response: mitigate – the junior developer pairs on sprint work, code is kept in a shared repository with notes, and contingency funds overtime if needed.

5 · Project Tracking & Dashboard

Trello board

The board uses Backlog → To Do → In Progress → Review → Done. Each card is one WBS work package with the same name as its ProjectLibre task, a due date taken from the ProjectLibre finish date and a priority label (red = critical path). At the status date, nine cards are Done, Sprint 2 is In Progress and overdue, the Sev-1 calendar fix and CR-04 consent check are in Review, and Sprint 3, notifications and training materials are ready in To Do. shows the daily workflow; ProjectLibre shows whether that workflow still meets the baseline dates.

6 · Integration & Final Management Recommendation

Our artefacts form one chain rather than separate tool outputs. The charter sets the scope; the scope is decomposed into the WBS; each work package becomes a ProjectLibre task with a duration, resource and cost, and a card with the same code. When Sprint 2 slipped, the same event appeared in (card still In Progress), ProjectLibre (80% complete on a critical task), the risk register (R02 occurring), the change register (CR-01 added effort, CR-03 rejected), the quality register (Q2 and Q7 in Attention) and finally the dashboard (SPI 0.90), which is what drives the management decision below.

Final management recommendation

Recommendation areaAssessment
Overall statusAmber – on budget, three working days behind on the critical path, recoverable.
ViabilityViable. CPI 0.98 forecasts labour at completion of about $36,265, well inside the $40,964 budget, and the remaining contingency can fund recovery.
Most important achievementRequirements, design and privacy review approved on time (M1, M2), and Sprint 1 delivered – the foundation is stable.
Most significant riskR02 double bookings: it strikes the system's core purpose and has already produced one Sev-1 defect.
Most significant schedule concernSprint 2 is +3 days on the critical path, threatening the 26 October go-live.
Stakeholder issueThe owner's frequent new requests (R01) – handled through the change register and weekly review, not informal agreement.
Major quality considerationNo open Sev-1 defects at go-live (Q7); UAT stays at four days (CR-03 rejected).
Recommended actionCrash Sprint 3 by three days (three paid Saturdays ≈ $1,440 from contingency, plus junior developer support using 3.4's float); re-baseline only if not recovered by M3 on 6 October.
Expected valueFewer missed enquiries, no double bookings, less admin time and a professional customer experience – measured by the share of bookings made online in the first three months.

Recommendation: continue the project. Approve the Sprint 3 recovery plan now and review at M3 (6 October).
